name: clone2
synopsis: int clone(int (*fn)(void *_Nullable), void *stack, int flags, void *_Nullable arg, ...);
long syscall(SYS_clone3, struct clone_args *cl_args, size_t size);
description: The clone system calls create a new child process similar to fork, but with more precise control over shared execution contexts such as memory, file descriptors, and signal handlers. This allows the child process to be placed in separate namespaces and share specific resources as specified.

parameters.name: fn
parameters.description: Function to be executed by the child process

parameters.name: stack
parameters.description: Pointer to the stack for the child process

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Bit mask of flags to control sharing and behavior

parameters.name: arg
parameters.description: Argument passed to the function fn

parameters.name: parent_tid
parameters.description: Optional pointer to store child TID in parent's memory

parameters.name: tls
parameters.description: Optional location of new thread-local storage

parameters.name: child_tid
parameters.description: Optional pointer to store child TID in child's memory

return_value.success: Returns the thread ID of the child process
return_value.failure: Returns -1, no child process is created, and errno is set to indicate the error

errors.description: CLONE_INTO_CGROUP specified but restrictions not met (clone3 only)
Too many processes are already running
CLONE_INTO_CGROUP specified but cgroup has a domain controller (clone3 only)
One or more PIDs in set_tid already exist (clone3 only)
Invalid flags or arguments specified, such as incompatible flag combinations
Insufficient memory to create the child process
Limit on nesting depth of namespaces exceeded
CLONE_INTO_CGROUP specified but cgroup is in invalid state (clone3 only)
Insufficient privileges for namespace creation or other operations

versions: Linux 2.0 and later, with extensions up to Linux 5.7 and beyond for clone3 features
